summary: Iteration-3 backend testing complete. Added /app/backend/tests/test_finance_approval.py (20 tests) covering role downgrade on register, /me scope fields, admin PATCH /auth/users, POST status workflow per role (admin auto-approved; manager/center_manager/partner/accountant pending; viewer 403), approve/reject endpoints, scoping on GET (center_manager by assigned_center_ids, partner by assigned_partner_id, accountant=all, viewer=own), status=pending filter, edit semantics, and dashboard include_pending toggle. Result: 19/20 iter-3 PASS + 21/21 iter-1 + 8/8 iter-2 regression PASS (48/49 overall). ONE REAL BUG: PUT /api/transactions/{id} by non-admin creator on an approved entry returns 403 instead of accepting the edit and resetting status to pending.

critical.issue: Non-admin creator cannot edit own *approved* entry — server returns 403 instead of accepting the update and resetting status='pending'. Spec says: 'editing approved entry by non-admin sets status back to pending'. The guard at server.py:560 requires existing.status=='pending' for non-admin, making the reset branch at lines 564-567 unreachable. Fix: drop the 'status==pending' requirement from the guard for the owner; keep the auto-reset to pending on save.

minor.issue: Empty/missing reason is silently coerced to ''. Consider requiring a non-empty reason (422) to preserve audit trail.
No validation that assigned_center_ids actually reference existing centers and assigned_partner_id references an existing partner. Stale IDs would silently scope a user to nothing.
Idempotency: re-approving an already-approved txn just updates approved_by/approved_at. Consider returning 409 or no-op semantics to avoid audit churn.
Scope filter for 'viewer' relies on created_by == user.id; a viewer who somehow has created_by data (legacy) could see unintended rows. Combine with explicit role check.

action_items: Fix PUT /api/transactions/{id}: allow non-admin creator to edit own approved entry; auto-reset status to pending (clear approved_by/approved_at). Currently returns 403, breaking the spec'd workflow.
Validate that PATCH /auth/users assigned_center_ids / assigned_partner_id reference real entities.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:560 — permission guard for PUT /transactions/{id} blocks non-admin owners on approved rows, making the 'reset-to-pending on edit' branch (lines 564-567) dead code. Spec violation.
Approve/Reject endpoints don't restrict by current status: rejected → approved is allowed without explicit transition validation. Consider a small state-machine guard.
TxnStatus enum strings 'pending'/'approved'/'rejected' are stored as-is in Mongo; no index on (status, created_by, center_id, partner_id) — GET /transactions will scan as the table grows.

POST /transactions returns status='approved' for admin but uses approved_at = datetime.utcnow().isoformat() in some paths and timezone-aware in others — be consistent (use timezone-aware UTC everywhere).

Self-register downgrade is correct, but PATCH /auth/users has no protection against an admin demoting themselves to viewer (could lock out the last admin). Consider 'cannot demote the last admin' check.

rca of the issue: Bug: PUT /api/transactions/{id} permission guard (server.py line 560) requires `existing.status == 'pending'` for non-admin owners. So when a center_manager who created a txn that admin later approved tries to PUT an edit, the guard rejects with 403. The follow-on branch (lines 564-567) that's supposed to reset status to pending is therefore unreachable for the very case it was written for. Fix: remove the `existing.status == 'pending'` clause from the owner-allow check; rely solely on (is_owner and role in editable_roles); keep the auto-reset block intact. Reproduction: (1) login as center_manager (assigned to centerX), POST /api/transactions for centerX → status=pending; (2) admin POST /transactions/{id}/approve → status=approved; (3) center_manager PUT /transactions/{id} with new amount → expected 200 + status=pending, actual 403 Forbidden.
